candidate.answerReason: There are 100 gaps of size 1/5 and therefore 101 terms. Fifty endpoint pairs sum to 60 each, with the middle term 30, giving 3030.

methods.label: Count the gaps and pair the terms
methods.explanation:
The terms increase by \(\frac15\), so first count the gaps from \(20\) to \(40\):
\[
\frac{40-20}{1/5}=100.
\]
Including both endpoints gives \(101\) terms.

Pair the first term with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and continue inward. In each pair, the increase from \(20\) matches the decrease from \(40\), so every pair sums to \(60\). The \(101\) terms form \(50\) pairs and leave the middle term, \(30\). Hence the sum is
\[
50\cdot60+30=\boxed{3030},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Counting equal increments and pairing terms give an elementary derivation of the arithmetic-series sum.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task target is summing a finite arithmetic sequence. The method uses the common difference to count terms with both endpoints included, then derives the sum by pairing opposite terms.
